brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack (a rack body to mount tools on)
requirements.evidence: Three full cells in a row (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) joined with joint bolts jointBolt:0#-1,0#0 and jointBolt:0#0,0#0, capped with capOpenFaces caps.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two hex-acc-keyhole Keyhole hangers on the back face (slot 1) of the two outer cells: accessory:0#-1,0#1 and accessory:0#1,0#1, spaced apart to hang the row on wall screws.
Three hex-acc-hook Hook plates (each carrying two hooks) on the opposite front face (slot 4) of all three cells: accessory:0#-1,0#4, accessory:0#0,0#4, accessory:0#1,0#4 — six hooks in total.

requirements.requirement: Staged hanging tools visible on the hooks
requirements.evidence: No staging props were placed: the only props that hang on a wall hook (cable coil, gaffer tape roll, FPV goggles) were refused with PROP_NO_REST because the single-storey rack sits on the bench and they would hang through it; small hand-tool props do not hang on these hooks per the configurator. The hooks themselves are present and empty, ready for real tools once wall-mounted.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell wall tool rack: a row of three full hex cells (left, centre, right) bolted together with lockJoints and finished with capOpenFaces caps. On the back face (slot 1) the two outer cells carry hex-acc-keyhole Keyhole hangers (accessory:0#-1,0#1, accessory:0#1,0#1) so the rack lifts and drops onto wall screws. On the front face (slot 4) all three cells carry hex-acc-hook Hook plates (accessory:0#-1,0#4, accessory:0#0,0#4, accessory:0#1,0#4), giving six hooks for small hand tools. check_build is clear with no issues. Staging props could not be hung: hanging props would pass through the bench at this single-storey height, so the hooks are shown empty.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
